1   SUMMARY                                                              
                                                                                     
            The purpose of this study was to test the efficacy of murine (B3) and humanized (LT3114)
            anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibodies in reducing pain behavior in a model of acute
            peripheral inflammatory hyperalgesia. Male Sprague Dawley rats were injected intraplantar
            in the left hindpaw with λ-carrageenan and then monitored for the presence of tactile
            allodynia over a period of 3 days, at which point injury typically resolves. Paw tactile
            sensitivity was assessed as the primary indicator of efficacy. Results showed that
            pretreatment with the NSAID k ...[truncated]

topics.title: Intravenous injection with PBS vehicle produces a small, transient reduction in threshold ...
topics.description:
Intravenous injection with PBS vehicle produces a small, transient reduction in threshold that
            is not significant. Intraplantar injection with λ-carrageenan produces a robust tactile
            allodynia as shown by a reduction in 50% gram threshold in rats that persists for at least
            72 hours (Figure 1).

This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted
            at the Department of Physiology and Pharmacology and Neuroscience, at the Karolinska
            Institute, (Stockholm, Sweden). The purpose of the study was to demonstrate efficacy of the
            murine anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibody (B3) to ameliorate CAIA-mediated
            mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity in the CAIA model.

topics.title: Therapeutic dosing with 10 mg/Kg B3 antibody (from Day 12 to Day ...
topics.description:
Therapeutic dosing with 10 mg/Kg B3 antibody (from Day 12 to Day 47) reversed
            CAIA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity beyond day 39 (time at which inflammation has
            completely resolved) (Figure 2B) with no effect on the degree of joint inflammation
            (Figure 2A). Treatment with control IgG (LT1015) or 40 mg/kg B3 had no impact on
            allodynia. (Figure 2B). Treatment with B3 antibody also reversed heat hypersensitivity in
            arthritic mice in both the inflammatory and the post-inflammatory phase (Figure 3A), but the
            
            antibody only attenuated CAIA-induced cold allodynia during the inflammatory phase at day
            19, and not at day 44 during the post-inflammatory phase (Figure 3B).

topics.title: 4.4 CONCLUSIONS The anti-LPA antibody, B3 increased the paw withdrawal threshold in ...
topics.description:
4.4  CONCLUSIONS                                                        
            The anti-LPA antibody, B3 increased the paw withdrawal threshold in diabetic rats to a level
            similar to that observed in non-diabetic rats, indicating a marked reduction in allodynia in
            rats with diabetes-induced neuropathic pain.                            
                                                                                     
            A single combined (i.t + i.v) dose of B3 was as effective as gabapentin in ameliorating
            established diabetic induced neuropathic pain.

This efficacy study in STZ induced diabetic rats was conducted at University of California San Diego
            (UCSD San Diego, CA). The purpose of this study was to determine the optimal dose level for the
            murine anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibody (B3) to reach long term reversal of allodynia in
            the STZ rat model of type 1 diabetes.

            when tested 3 days after drug delivery, indicating a sustained and specific effect of drug that
            washes out in approximately two weeks after treatments are stopped.

1   SUMMARY                                                              
                                                                                     
            In a preliminary study in a rat paclitaxel induced neuropathic pain model (1 mg/kg paclitaxel
            intraperitoneally, every other day for 4 doses) the efficacy of the murine anti-S1P antibody
            and the anti-LPA antibody (504B3) was examined in comparison with their respective
            isotype control antibodies (LT1017 and LT1015). Antibodies were dosed intravenously
            (25 mg/kg) one day prior to the first injection of paclitaxel and then at days 2, 5, 8, 11 and
            14 after the first paclitaxel injection. Mechanical allodynia was measured by automated von
            Frey testing. P ...[truncated]

topics.title: 4 CONCLUSIONS Paclitaxel caused the development of mechanical allodynia as compared with ...
topics.description:
4   CONCLUSIONS                                                         
                                                                                     
            Paclitaxel caused the development of mechanical allodynia as compared with control animals
            and this allodynia was significantly reduced by administration of LT1002 and 504B3 while
            the isotype control produced no effect on mechanical allodynia.

This efficacy study in STZ induced diabetic rats was conducted at University of California San Diego

            murine anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibody (B3) to reach long term reversal of allodynia in
            the STZ rat model of type 1 diabetes.

topics.description:
Results showed
            that anti-LPA antibody at 10 and 30 mg/kg increased the paw withdrawal threshold in
            diabetic rats when compared to IgG control or vehicle treated animals to a level similar to
            that observed in non-diabetic rats. This marked reduction in mechanical allodynia is observed
            when tested 3 days after drug delivery, indicating a sustained and specific effect of drug that
            washes out in approximately two weeks after treatments are stopped.

topics.title: This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted ...
topics.description:
This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted
            at the Department of Physiology and Pharmacology and Neuroscience, at the Karolinska
            Institute, (Stockholm, Sweden). The purpose of the study was to demonstrate efficacy of the
            murine anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibody (B3) to ameliorate CAIA-mediated
            mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity in the CAIA model.

            determine the efficacy of anti-LPA antibody treatment in relieving chronic non-inflammatory
            pain in the CAIA model.

            hypersensitivity at day 14, but had no effect on the arthritis clinical score (Figure 1B).

topics.title: Therapeutic dosing with 10 mg/Kg B3 antibody (from Day 12 to Day ...
topics.description:
Therapeutic dosing with 10 mg/Kg B3 antibody (from Day 12 to Day 47) reversed
            CAIA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity beyond day 39 (time at which inflammation has
            completely resolved) (Figure 2B) with no effect on the degree of joint inflammation
            (Figure 2A). Treatment with control IgG (LT1015) or 40 mg/kg B3 had no impact on
            allodynia. (Figure 2B). Treatment with B3 antibody also reversed heat hypersensitivity in
            arthritic mice in both the inflammatory and the post-inflammatory phase (Figure 3A), but the
            
            antibody only attenuated CAIA-induced cold allodynia during the inflammatory phase at day
            19, and not at day 44 during the post-inflammatory phase (Figure 3B).

topics.title: This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted ...
topics.description:
This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted
            at the Department of Physiology and Pharmacology and Neuroscience, at the Karolinska
            Institutet, (Stockholm, Sweden). The purpose of the study was to test the effect of a two
            doses of a murine anti-LPA antibody (B3), to examine the duration of protection once
            treatment was stopped, and to determine whether B3 could be effective when the start of
            treatment was delayed until all inflammation had resolved.

In summary, a murine anti-LPA antibody (B3) decreased tactile hypersensitivity in arthritic
            mice in a dose dependent fashion and B3 therapy was highly effective when delayed until
            mechanical hypersensitivity was well established and all signs of inflammation had
            disappeared in the disease model.

topics.title: 1 SUMMARY This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model ...
topics.description:
1   SUMMARY                                                             
                                                                                     
            This efficacy study in the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model was conducted
            at the Department of Physiology and Pharmacology and Neuroscience, at the Karolinska
            Institutet, (Stockholm, Sweden). The purpose of the study was to test the effect of a two
            doses of a murine anti-LPA antibody (B3), to examine the duration of protection once
            treatment was stopped, and to determine whether B3 could be effective when the start of
            treatment was delayed until all inflammation had resolved. ...[truncated]

topics.title: Thus, this study was designed to test the effect of two doses ...
topics.description:
Thus, this
            study was designed to test the effect of two doses (2 and 10 mg/Kg) of antibody, to examine
            the duration of the protection once treatment was stopped, and to determine whether antibody
            could be effective when the start of treatment was delayed until all inflammation had
            resolved i.e. to demonstrate a therapeutic effect of antibody treatment that was not solely as a
            result of blocking the onset of allodynia in this model.

topics.title: Thus, studies were undertaken to determine the efficacy of anti-LPA antibody treatment ...

Thus, studies were undertaken to determine the
            efficacy of anti-LPA antibody treatment in relieving chronic non-inflammatory pain in the
            CAIA model.

Treatment with B3 resulted in reduction of tactile hypersensitivity (Figure 1b.) with a no
            specific, small effect on arthritis score at the lower dose of antibody treatment (Figure 1a.).
            No significant differences were observed between CAIA Saline and 1015 treated animals
            (Figure 1b). After 12 days of treatment with 10 mg/kg, animals receiving B3 were
            indistinguishable from “no CAIA” control animals. B3 at 2 mg/kg was partially effective
            whereas control antibody had no effect on tactile hypersensitivity (Figure 1). When treatment
            of the 10 mg/kg group was stopped at D43 a gradual decrease in protection was seen that
            paralleled the expected time course for loss of B3 from circulation (blue line in Figure 1 a ...[truncated]

topics.title: In summary, this study demonstrated elevation of LPA in diabetic animals and ...
topics.description:
In summary, this study demonstrated elevation of LPA in diabetic animals and that a single
            dose of B3 was sufficient to ameliorate the tactile hypersensitivity measured in these animals.
            In addition, B3 reduced the concentration of LPA in the plasma and this reduction correlated
            with the extent of efficacy seen.

topics.title: 1 SUMMARY The purpose of this study was to evaluate if LPA ...
topics.description:
1   SUMMARY                                                              
                                                                                     
            The purpose of this study was to evaluate if LPA was upregulated in a model of STZ-induced
            diabetes in the rat. Preliminary efficacy of an anti-LPA antibody was also examined.

topics.title: In diabetic rats that were allodynic, levels of LPA were elevated in ...
topics.description:
In diabetic rats that were allodynic, levels of LPA were elevated in the plasma (Figure 1) and
            the dorsal root ganglia (Figure 2) in comparison with normal control rats. Staining in the
            dorsal root ganglia of diabetic rats was specific to the presence of LPA as shown by the lack
            of staining in these samples of a non-specific control antibody (Figure 2).

topics.title: These data demonstrate that blocking the activity of LPA with a single ...
topics.description:

            antibody is sufficient to ameliorate neuropathic pain in the rat STZ-induced model of diabetic
            neuropathy and that the reduction in pain is accompanied by a decrease in LPA levels that are
            upregulated in the vehicle group.

topics.title: Animals treated with LT3114 at 10 mg/kg showed a significant effect on ...
topics.description:
Animals treated with LT3114 at 10 mg/kg showed a significant effect on the wound
               healing process in terms of accelerated wound closure compared with vehicle treated
               animals but demonstrated no change in tensile strength of the healed wound. Animals
               treated with LT3114 at 50 mg/kg also exhibited significant improvement of wound
               closure compared with vehicle treated animals but no change in tensile strength.

topics.title: Based on the results, LT3114 at 10 mg/kg seems to exhibit an ...
topics.description:
Based on the results,
               LT3114 at 10 mg/kg seems to exhibit an effect on the inflammation phase based on the
               percent wound closure, whereas it had no effect on the maturation or remodeling phase as
               measured by tensile strength. However, effects of LT3114 on inflammation need to be
               further confirmed by histological evaluation (e.g. dermal gap and dermal hyperplasia).

topics.title: Concentrations of LT3114 in plasma collected at the end of study were ...
topics.description:
Concentrations of LT3114 in plasma collected at the end of study were assayed by both
               human IgG quantification or by binding ELISA. All animals had quantifiable
               concentrations in the plasma and in general the two methods of quantification were
                                                                                     
               similar. However there was no dose response noted for LT3114 between 10 to 50 mg/kg.

          10 µg/mL to a full panel of human tissues based on recommendations in Annex II of Directive
          75/318/EEC, “Production and Quality Control of Monoclonal Antibodies” and in the 1997 US FDA/CBER

          evaluated.

                                    color intensity is proportional to the quantity of LT3114.

Rat serum samples, positive controls and negative controls were diluted 1:30 in assay buffer
            and then incubated at room temperature for 60±10 minutes in the presence of Biotinylated
            LT3114 and Ruthenylated-LT3114 with additional dilution of 1:3. The antibodies (IgG,
            IgM, etc.) resulted in the bridging of biotinylated and ruthenylated-LT3114. After
            incubation, 50 μL of each mixture is added to the wells of the Streptavidin coated MSD plate
            and allowed to bind for 60±10 minutes. In the presence of tripropylamine-containing read
            buffer, ruthenium produces a chemiluminescent signal that is triggered when voltage is
            applied. The resulting chemiluminescence is measured in response unit (RU) on SECTOR ...[truncated]

topics.title: Cannulated male Sprague Dawley rats received a 10 mg/kg IV bolus dose ...
topics.description:
Cannulated male Sprague Dawley rats received a 10 mg/kg IV bolus dose of a single
            humanized anti-LPA antibody (LT3114, LT3211, LT3212 or LT3611). Serial blood samples
            were collected from an implanted femoral vein cannula for up to 21 days post dosing for
            determination of anti-LPA antibody plasma concentrations. Plasma concentrations of
            humanized anti-LPA antibody were quantified using a direct-binding ELISA. PK data
            analysis using noncompartmental methods (software package WinNonlin version 5.3
            (Pharsight, Inc.; Mountain View, CA) was conducted.

topics.title: This pharmacokinetic (PK) study in Sprague-Dawley rats was conducted at Biotox Sciences ...
topics.description:
This pharmacokinetic (PK) study in Sprague-Dawley rats was conducted at Biotox Sciences
            (San Diego, CA) and Lpath (San Diego, CA). The purpose of this study was to establish the
            systemic concentrations of humanized anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) antibodies in the rat
            dosed by an intravenous (IV) route of administration. Measuring these concentrations will
            allow calculation of several pharmacokinetic parameters useful in further development of
            these antibodies.

topics.title: LT3211 plasma concentrations were measurable for up to 6 days post IV ...
topics.description:
LT3211 plasma concentrations were measurable for up to 6 days post IV bolus dosing of
            10 mg/kg LT3211. LT3211 concentrations declined in a bi-exponential fashion with the
            initial phase lasting for up to one to two days after administration of a 10 mg/kg IV bolus.
            LT3211 plasma concentrations declined about seven to ten-fold from 30 minutes to two days
            post IV bolus dosing. Thereafter, LT3211 plasma concentrations declined to non-measurable
            concentrations within two weeks post IV bolus dosing with an approximate terminal half-life
            of 5 days. Mean LT3211 plasma concentrations at 30 minutes were 181 µg/mL and the mean
            AUC    was 3.94 mg.h/mL.
